what_it_is.prose: The Airbus A400M Atlas is a European four-engine turboprop strategic/tactical airlifter (roughly 37-tonne payload, powered by four Europrop TP400-D6 engines) operated by several NATO and other air forces. It is NOT in Indian service, has no Indian order and no Indian industrial partner. Its only India relevance is as a nominal contender in the Indian Air Force's Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme; however, it is widely reported to have effectively fallen out of contention because its ~37-tonne capacity is substantially larger than the MTA's 18–30-tonne requirement and its acquisition and lifecycle costs are seen as prohibitive — 'multiple medium transports could be acquired for the price of a single Atlas.' The front-runners in that competition are the Embraer C-390 (with Mahindra) and the Lockheed Martin C-130J-30 (with Tata). This dossier is deliberately a short Tier C stub: it documents the absence of an A400M India footprint honestly rather than inferring one.
